title: Card Game Harness for playtesting: The State v.
author: Fairway3Games
selftext:
Let me start here: I wrote down all of my rules, cards, card effects, starting conditions and victory conditions.  I did not use AI as my 'creative' partner. I used AI (openai work) as my technical implementation.

I had a card game idea: a deck builder in which you are a defense attorney building a case for your client who's accused of a crime.  There's fewer than 60 total cards that I created in a spreadsheet.

I then gave my agent the [rules](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mAZpnGkei9yAc9sji-Bo0SeuHveP--AqMbn5PGuk3U4/edit?usp=drive_link), a spreadsheet of cards, and a lot of implementation specifications. I asked it to build an AI game test harness for the new game. It lets me rapidly test the game, make rules changes, update cards.   It implements and enforces the rules, has a tutorial for new players, and it tracks EACH play through. I can literally get a full replay.

https://i.redd.it/cii8n2rquz3i1.png

I have created a card editor to help me quickly iterate and test new cards.

https://i.redd.it/m6gyy7eavz3i1.png

I have a generic playtest framework that shows me card choices, turn times, etc.  I can watch the replay. I can see popular and unpopular cards. I can see how many games get started and never finish.

https://i.redd.it/21qxco6zuz3i1.png

The process of putting this together in a different time line would be months. I could create the whole harness in days.

I didn't, in anyway, give up my creativity as a designer. It let me bring it to fruition, quickly.  I will be able to tell if this concept has merit a lot faster.  I didn't spend weeks putting together handwritten cards, futzing with ugly early prototypes, etc.  

You can try the game yourself: https://defense.fairway3games.com.
